_doc: T4 recorded exceptions to the golden records. Regenerated 2026-07-29 with the P5 dependency-loss fixes in place. Every entry pins old -> new and expires the moment the goldens are recaptured (test_bug_ledger_entries_are_live). STRUCTURAL only: the T2 movement is NOT laundered through the ledger -- it is the delta table under review in docs/rewrite/restructure/REBASELINE.md.

entries.justification: P5 CONTROL-TRANSFER SUBSET, re-justified 2026-07-29. build() emits fewer 1-BYTE CONTROL send/recv pairs than legacy; every PAYLOAD transfer, every collective, every compute op and every compute-microsecond total is identical. TWO causes, both now measured rather than assumed. (1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

entries.justification: P5-ZERO3-CROSS-STAGE-SYNC (2026-07-29). Rows S8/S15 anchor a ZeRO-3 parameter gather on layer (l - prefetch_depth), which at a stage boundary is a layer on the OTHER pipeline stage, so the gather inherits a foreign rank's deps and is inherited as a foreign rank's dep. Legacy materialized all EIGHT such edges as zero-byte cross_layer_rank0 TransferOps, but only the four whose consumer sat on dst_device produced a RECV; the other four emitted UNPAIRED SENDs that nothing waits on (golden SEND:1=16, RECV:1=8). et_emit used to DROP all eight with a CrossRankDepWarning justified by 'the ordering is carried by the shared per-stage collectives' -- which is false: the gather's communicator is stage 1's dp pair and its dep is on stage 0, and NO collective has members on both stages. The four dropped dep-side edges were the only thing ordering the gathers, which became graph ROOTS issuing at t=0 (+1.366%). Emission is TOTAL now: all eight go on the wire as PAIRED 1-byte control pairs, so the emitted DAG equals the IR the analytical evaluator honors. SEND:1 is therefore IDENTICAL to golden (16); RECV:1 is 16 vs golden 8 -- the eight legacy SENDs that carried no ordering now carry it, at a cost of 5 microseconds (+0.002%, was +1.366%). The underlying cross-stage anchor is filed as BUG_LEDGER A6 and is NOT fixed here; fixing it is a modeling change that moves the analytical golden.

entries.justification: P5 CONTROL-TRANSFER SUBSET, re-justified 2026-07-29. build() emits fewer 1-BYTE CONTROL send/recv pairs than legacy; every PAYLOAD transfer, every collective, every compute op and every compute-microsecond total is identical. TWO causes, both now measured rather than assumed. (1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

(1) ONE p2p IS ONE IDENTITY: legacy_lowering recorded same_device_edges per (edge, same-stage source parent) and Step 11 created one TransferOp per key, so a logical p2p whose producer chain ended in a collective became TWO ops with TWO tags. build() emits one object, and its SEND now carries BOTH producers as ctrl_deps (et_emit Phase B), so the merge is ordering-neutral -- which is what it was NOT before this commit (the compute anchor was dropped, which is what moved T2 by up to -5.945%). (2) R3 IS PER DEVICE (INTERFACES 4.3): legacy attached the COARSE cross-microbatch GPipe boundary to EVERY cluster rank of a stage and lowered each cross-device pair to a zero-byte control message; build() records the boundary as a device-local dep. This is a REMOVED OVER-CONSTRAINT, not a re-encoding: the removed cross-cluster-rank orderings are NOT implied by any surviving path (proved by closure comparison; see REBASELINE 4.2), and they are the whole of the residual T2 movement on this spec (-0.116% to -0.215%). Derived fields (ops_hash/n_nodes/critical_path*/manifest*/bytes_by_kind[SEND|RECV]/byte_hist/bytes_by_axis[p2p]/n_transfers/n_recv) move with those counts. critical_path_* also moves because R2 now STATES the microbatch's SOFTMAX/FORWARD->SOFTMAX/BACKWARD and LAYER/FORWARD->RECOMPUTE edges (INTERFACES 4.3 amendment 2026-07-29); those orderings were already implied, so the AstraSim wall clock does not move with them. Evidence: every bundle completes under equiv.dlsim, p2p tags pair bijectively, the group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold, and AstraSim runs all 42 specs.
entries.dlsim_evidence: equiv.dlsim: bundle completes; p2p tags pair bijectively; group-order and no-lost-successor postconditions hold

entries.justification: P5-GID-NUMBERING. comm_groups.json gids 1000..1003 hold the member sets [0],[2],[1],[3] instead of [0],[1],[2],[3]. All four are SINGLETONS (the ep-axis communicator of a COARSE program, whose device space carries no ep axis -- ABSENT_AXIS_SINGLETON_GROUP), and a singleton wire group is emitted as a zero-duration *_noop COMP, never as a collective (Class B 10g). The SET of member sets is unchanged; only which gid each interned under moved, because gids are allocated in sorted-label order and labels are now assigned in program order. collectives_by_group -- the T1 quantity keyed on the member set rather than the gid -- is identical.

BUG_LEDGER A3, which INTERFACES 7 records as 'already impossible' in the new design: legacy's OVERLAP_NODE_COPY_ATTRS omitted is_moe_layer, so the head of a tp-overlap split MoE layer was filed under DENSE and the memory census counted the same layer twice. build() derives every field of a split op from the same WorkItem, so the flag cannot be lost. The ledger's predicted direction and shape hold exactly: the reported peak DECREASES by one dense layer's worth per split MoE layer per device. Timing unaffected.
